country.name: Bolivia
country.languagePolicy: Spanish is a default interface language, not the only official language. Localization involving the official languages of Indigenous Original Peasant Nations and Peoples requires community, linguistic, territorial and institutional review; automatic translation is not reviewed localization.

review.policy: No category becomes verified without a named qualified Bolivian reviewer, current authoritative sources and review of the responsible national, departmental, district, community, institution or program authority.

governanceModel.summary: Bolivia's Plurinational Education System is governed nationally by the Ministry of Education and implemented through departmental and district education structures. The base curriculum is complemented by regionalized and diversified curricula developed with Indigenous Original Peasant Nations and Peoples. Public autonomous universities and private or special-regime institutions have different legal and program-recognition pathways.
governanceModel.nationalAuthority: Ministerio de Educación del Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia
governanceModel.schoolRule: Preserve the education-unit code, name, geographic area, dependency, level, department, province, municipality, district, reporting year, source date and review date.
governanceModel.higherEducationRule: Public-university autonomy or membership in the Bolivian University System, private-university institutional authorization, official validity of a particular academic program, degree issuance and program accreditation are distinct claims.

authorities.name: Ministerio de Educación
authorities.role: national education authority, base curriculum, education-unit registry and private higher-education regulation

authorities.name: Direcciones Departamentales and Distritales de Educación
Sistema de Información Educativa — SEIE/SIE
authorities.role: education-unit directory, infrastructure records, statistics and indicators

authorities.name: Dirección General de Educación Superior Universitaria
authorities.role: higher-education policy and official validity of programs at private institutions within its competence

authorities.name: Comité Ejecutivo de la Universidad Boliviana
authorities.role: coordination of the autonomous public Bolivian University System and its internal academic framework

authorities.name: Defensoría de la Niñez y Adolescencia
authorities.role: municipal child and adolescent protection services under the applicable legal framework

curriculum.title: Currículo Base del Sistema Educativo Plurinacional and current subsystem guidance
curriculum.implementationRule: Confirm subsystem, level, field or area, publication version, current annual guidance, applicable regionalized and diversified curriculum, language and community context before mapping a resource.
curriculum.supplementPolicy: External materials may supplement but never silently replace the base curriculum, approved regionalized or diversified curriculum, annual implementation guidance or community knowledge framework.

schoolDirectory.authority: Ministerio de Educación through SEIE/SIE, with territorial education structures
schoolDirectory.scopeNotice: SEIE permits searches by education unit, geography, area, dependency and level and displays a management year. Directory information is referential; a listing does not by itself prove current authorization for every level, shift, building or service.

educationStatistics.scopeNotice: Every figure must display management year, publication or update date, measure, population, geography, dependency, source and filters. Historical series affected by registry cleaning or definition changes must carry the relevant methodological note.

higherEducation.ministryAuthority: Dirección General de Educación Superior Universitaria
higherEducation.publicUniversitySystem: Comité Ejecutivo de la Universidad Boliviana
higherEducation.authorityNotice: Autonomous public-university status or CEUB membership, private-university institutional authorization, official validity for a particular program, campus and modality, degree authority, and time-bound program accreditation such as ARCU-SUR are distinct. Each claim must identify the authority, decision, scope, date and current status.

privacyAndSafeguarding.constitutionalAndSectorReview: Bolivia does not yet have a generally enacted comprehensive personal-data law equivalent to a modern omnibus regime identified in the reviewed official sources. Applicable constitutional, habeas-data, education, child, telecommunications, financial and other sector rules require qualified review.
privacyAndSafeguarding.pendingBillNotice: PL 538/2025-2026 is listed as a bill in treatment and must not be presented as enacted law.
privacyAndSafeguarding.childrenLaw: Ley N.º 548, Código Niña, Niño y Adolescente, as amended
privacyAndSafeguarding.scopeNotice: The absence of a confirmed comprehensive statute is not permission to process learner data. Data minimization, lawful authority, child safeguards, consent or authorization, security, incident handling and local institutional protocols require qualified Bolivian review before real learner participation.

culturalAndLanguageRequirements.rule: The base curriculum must be harmonized with applicable regionalized and diversified curricula in coordination with the relevant Indigenous Original Peasant Nations and Peoples. Language, knowledge, territorial and community requirements cannot be inferred nationally or replaced by automatic translation.

completionCriteria: A qualified Bolivian education reviewer is named.
National, departmental, district and community responsibilities are reviewed for the participating institution.
Every education-unit record preserves code, dependency, level, geography, management year, source date and review date.
Every statistic shows management year, update date, definition, geography, population and provenance, including methodological breaks.
Every higher-education claim distinguishes public autonomy or CEUB membership, private institutional authorization, program validity, campus, modality, degree authority and accreditation.
Curriculum mappings identify subsystem, level, area, version, annual guidance and applicable regionalized or diversified curriculum.
Official-language and Indigenous Original Peasant community requirements are reviewed with competent community participation.
The personal-data legal gap, applicable constitutional and sector rules, and child-protection requirements are reviewed by qualified Bolivian counsel; bills are not presented as law.
Privacy, safeguarding, accessibility, incident and consent procedures are approved by each participating institution.
No authorization, recognition, accreditation, partnership or credential claim exceeds documentary evidence.
